prompt: Replace this proposed payment-data platform: write the order database and Kafka separately; retry every timeout with a new event ID; call Kafka exactly once; accept any JSON and repair it later; use Redis as the read authority; alert only on broker health and host CPU; scale consumers without inspecting partitions; let failed data-quality checks continue publishing; back up the database without restoring it; and claim zero RPO/RTO from a successful local demo. Produce a safer transactional, streaming, analytical, observability, capacity, security and recovery design with executable evidence gates.
directAnswer: Keep the order and atomic outbox in one database transaction, relay with stable event identity and expect duplicate publication. Validate a versioned event contract at ingress, contain incompatible records without logging sensitive payloads and process valid events with an atomic inbox/effect transaction. Treat Kafka as retained transport, PostgreSQL as source/effect authority and Redis as disposable. Partition by an explicit ordering and distribution requirement, measure per-partition lag plus age and model throughput/headroom. Reconcile source and fact identities, counts and monetary totals; fail publication on material quality errors and retain lineage receipts. Trace one operation with low-cardinality identifiers and privacy controls. Encrypt and authorize each boundary in reachable deployments. Define state-class backup and replay procedures, verify signed backup integrity, restore into an isolated target, reconcile and measure declared RPO/RTO. Do not convert local evidence into production guarantees.
foundation: Distributed reliability comes from explicit ownership and recovery contracts, not from a product name. A database transaction cannot atomically commit to an unrelated broker without a protocol. Delivery can repeat, ordering is partition-scoped, schemas evolve, derived stores drift and backups are only useful when restorable. SLOs and recovery objectives are promises with eligibility and measured evidence.
reasoningSteps: Define the business operation, source of truth, acceptable duplicate behavior, ordering scope, freshness objective and loss boundary.
Commit order, idempotency key, request hash and outbox event atomically in PostgreSQL.
Return the same result for an identical idempotency retry and reject key reuse with changed intent.
Relay the stable outbox identity to Kafka and acknowledge publication separately, accepting the publish-before-ack duplicate window.
Version the event envelope and payload; test backward/forward compatibility before producer rollout.
Validate keys and payload identity before business processing; quarantine only minimal metadata for incompatible records.
Commit consumer inbox and business effect in one transaction; reject same event identity with changed payload hash.
Update or rebuild Redis only after the durable effect, with TTL, memory bound and explicit stale/miss behavior.
Choose partition keys from ordering and cardinality needs; measure end offsets, processed offsets, age, skew and per-partition rate.
Set capacity from arrival rate, service rate, failure headroom and recovery time rather than aggregate CPU.
Build facts from governed inputs and block publication when identity, count, control-total, null, duplicate or freshness gates fail.
Persist lineage receipts with run identity, code/config identity, input/output datasets, watermarks, metrics and status.
Instrument the user journey across API, transaction, relay, broker, consumer, database and analytical job without high-cardinality metric labels.
Protect reachable endpoints with authenticated identities, least privilege, encryption, secret rotation and audit logging that excludes sensitive payloads.
Separate database authority, retained log, derived facts and cache in the recovery inventory.
Hash and inventory backups, restore into an isolated target, replay from compatible retained watermarks and reconcile before promotion.
Declare RPO/RTO and SLO measurement windows before tests; publish observed local results with hardware and topology limits.
Exercise dependency loss, duplicate delivery, poison input, skew, stale cache, quality failure and restore refusal in bounded tests.
Define incident roles, stop conditions, rollback/roll-forward decisions and evidence preservation.
Require an independent reviewer to inject unfamiliar faults and sign observable rubric evidence before any capability claim.
seniorAnswer: I would begin with one traceable payment operation and explicit state ownership. PostgreSQL atomically stores the order, idempotency decision and outbox. A relay publishes a stable event ID and may repeat after a publish-before-ack crash; Kafka retention is not described as exactly-once business processing. The consumer validates a versioned contract and atomically stores inbox identity plus effect, making replay harmless while detecting identity conflicts. Redis is a bounded projection rebuilt after durable commits. Partitioning follows ordering and distribution requirements, and capacity uses per-partition arrival/service rates, lag age and failure headroom. The analytical pipeline reconciles identities, rows and money, records lineage and blocks release on material failures or unresolved quarantine. Metrics remain low cardinality; traces/logs carry sampled correlation under privacy controls. Recovery inventory distinguishes source database, event retention, facts and cache. Every backup is hashed, restored to a separate target, replayed from recorded watermarks and reconciled before any switch. The local test can report its measured snapshot equality and restore duration, but not zero production RPO/RTO, HA or capacity. An independent transfer review and ongoing restore drills are required.
weakAnswer: Enable Kafka idempotence, add more consumers, store everything in Redis for speed, send bad messages to a dead-letter topic and take daily snapshots. Grafana green means the platform is reliable.
whyWeak: It substitutes features for end-to-end guarantees, ignores source/broker dual writes, stable identities, effect idempotency, schema governance, partition limits, quality blocking, privacy, restore validation and truthful objective scope.

evidence.signal: A forced crash after broker acknowledgement and before outbox acknowledgement produces two offsets with one event ID and one effect.
evidence.proves: The tested relay can duplicate delivery while the tested inbox/effect path remains idempotent.
evidence.doesNotProve: Every producer/consumer implementation or external side effect is exactly once.

evidence.signal: Nine records map to one partition, lag rises to nine and returns to zero after processing.
evidence.proves: The key hash, per-partition telemetry and bounded consumer drain behave as observed.
evidence.doesNotProve: Production throughput, balanced real keys or unlimited catch-up capacity.

evidence.signal: A quality run fails with nine missing facts, then passes with equal counts and monetary totals.
evidence.proves: The declared reconciliation gate detects and later clears that controlled gap.
evidence.doesNotProve: Semantic correctness of every field or every downstream dataset.

evidence.signal: An incompatible event records only ID, offset, hash and reason while processing continues.
evidence.proves: The implemented consumer contains that schema failure without copying raw payload into quarantine.
evidence.doesNotProve: The event has been resolved, retention is safe or all sensitive data is absent from every other log.

evidence.signal: A hashed dump restores into an isolated database, replay reconciles and the second restore refuses overwrite.
evidence.proves: That snapshot and retained log recover the bounded fixture within the observed local time.
evidence.doesNotProve: Production RPO/RTO, failover, cross-region durability or recovery of events outside recorded retention.

followUps.answer: It can reduce broker duplicates for a producer session, but it does not atomically commit a business database and Kafka, nor make a consumer's database or external side effect exactly once.
No. Unsupported schemas need ownership, classification, compatibility correction and governed replay. Blind retry creates hot loops, cost and alert noise without changing the invalid input.

followUps.prompt: How should partition count be changed?
followUps.answer: Through a compatibility plan covering key-to-partition changes, ordering expectations, consumer state, replay, downstream assumptions, staged exposure and rollback or roll-forward. Adding partitions can change key placement.

followUps.prompt: What makes a data-quality gate operationally safe?
followUps.answer: Clear ownership, severity, bounded checks, reproducible metrics, fail/hold behavior, exception governance, lineage receipts and a recovery path that does not edit evidence to make the gate green.

followUps.prompt: When can Redis be used during database recovery?
followUps.answer: As supporting evidence or a disposable acceleration layer if its staleness is understood. It should not silently become the authoritative source unless the architecture explicitly provides equivalent durability and correctness guarantees.

followUps.prompt: What is the honest recovery claim after one local restore?
followUps.answer: The named synthetic snapshot restored and reconciled within the observed time on that topology. Production objectives remain unproved until representative scale, failure domains, people, dependencies and repeated drills are tested.

rubric.observableEvidence: Uses idempotency plus atomic source/outbox and explains the relay ambiguity.
Uses stable identity, versioned contracts, inbox/effect atomicity and conflict detection.
Connects ordering, key distribution, lag age, throughput and failure headroom.
Defines blocking identity/count/control-total/freshness gates and lineage receipts.
Separates source, retained log, facts and disposable cache semantics.
Traces the journey, avoids cardinality traps and defines eligible freshness/correctness objectives.
Applies least privilege, encryption, secret hygiene and payload-safe logs/quarantine.
Uses signed backup, isolated restore, retained replay, reconciliation and overwrite refusal.
Defines evidence preservation, bounded faults, stop conditions and reversible recovery.
Distinguishes local receipts from HA, capacity, production and mastery claims.
